note: The vocabulary gate's exceptions (tools/src/gates/check-vocabulary.ts reads it; nothing generates from it). An entry is { name, match, reason, owner, since }: match is an exact path or a whole-path glob, and the entry excuses every banned phrasing in the markdown files it matches. A banned phrasing is a failure, never a category, so every entry owes an owner and a since date, and a whole run fails an entry that excuses nothing, so an exception cannot outlive its cause. The one entry excuses the working plan's own wording until its work lands (plans/harness-optimize.md), against exceptions-C8 (an excusing list ships empty) as context-layers.json does; once no plan uses a banned phrasing, it excuses nothing and must be deleted. The fixture trees, changelogs and dated records are left out by the gate itself, and a single line opts out with <!-- vocab-ok -->; neither needs an entry. Edit this file, then run: make gate G=check-vocabulary.

entries.name: working-plans
entries.reason: A working plan records its decisions in the words of their day, and is deleted or moved into docs/ when its work lands; it describes a migration in flight, not the repo as it is (plans/ is exempt from the context layers for the same reason).
